proof_attempt_summary: The run established the fixed-T cohort-mean cycle geometry, canonical bound and attaining estimator, exact codimension-q exceptional covariance laws, and bounded realizable strict-loss witnesses; it also proved q>0 nonuniversality for the Moreau--Kastler estimator on the exact balanced intersection. The field-tier claim collapsed because the unrestricted individual-level frontier, q=0 individual result, application-matching controls/dependence, and growing-horizon theory were not delivered; a local-DQM regularity argument and related-work cleanup also remain before reusing the strongest efficiency wording.
tldr: At fixed \(T\), with a never-treated cohort, positive multiplicative untreated means, mutually independent cohort samples, arbitrary within-unit dependence, and finite fourth moments, one weighted tangent restriction arises from each untreated graph cycle. Bounded score truncation followed by an exact mean adjustment proves tangent completeness in the explicitly mean-differentiable experiment. The canonical gradient removes the covariance projection of the cohort-mean PPML influence onto the \(q\) cycle directions; a feasible cycle-projection estimator attains the bound and supports pointwise Wald inference. The cohort-mean PPML estimator is efficient for every bounded legal covariance law exactly when \(q=0\); for \(q>0\), exactly \(q\) primitive balances characterize its exceptional efficient laws, and a bounded strictly positive fixed-support family has exact loss \(\Gamma>0\). On the balanced equal-weight, no-covariate, no-offset intersection with Moreau--Kastler, the individual and cohort-mean point estimators coincide, so the same family and the regular cycle-projection competitor prove that the published individual estimator is not universally efficient when \(q>0\). This transfer is one-way: it gives neither the richer individual-level efficiency bound nor a \(q=0\) efficiency conclusion there. The regularized frontier for growing \(T\) and \(q\) remains open at \(\mathrm{oeq{:}growing\text{-}cycle\text{-}frontier}\).
gap: Moreau--Kastler (2025) fits untreated individual fixed effects and aggregates individual counterfactual predictions into PTT, while Wooldridge (2023) develops fully interacted individual-level nonlinear imputation for cohort--time average treatment effects. Neither provides an efficiency frontier for the distinct cohort-mean rank-one PPML score; existing efficient staggered-DiD results are additive, and rank-one completion results do not classify causal-estimator efficiency.
fill: The project proves weighted-cycle tangent completeness by a support-preserving score construction, derives and attains the canonical gradient with explicit sample covariance functionals, differentiates the cohort-mean PPML-imputation estimator, characterizes its efficient covariance laws by \(q\) primitive balances, and certifies strict loss on a realizable bounded family and a positive-radius ambient covariance neighborhood. A boundary proposition supplies the exact profiling conditions under which the Moreau--Kastler individual estimator collapses to the cohort-mean estimator.
